notes.title: Mental Prep and Pedal Technique
notes.raw_capture: Anxiety and performance jitters presenting themselves when playing without obvious connection to conscious thought. Observation is that Richard has a lot of criticality and judgement in his mental assessment during playing - which may lead to difficulty in activating muscle memory effectively.
notes.cleaned_text: Hey Richard, Really appreciate the session and moving to a more official structure for your music growth. The first half of our session was spent on mental preparation and psychological tools to better connect your musicality to expression when playing. The second half was more on pedal and fingering technique. Recommendation is to focus on an emotional representation of the piece internally that can act as a bridge to have the conscious mind support the subconscious player. Strong internal perception whether visual (space cloud with asteroids) or kinaesthetic (plastic bag with warmth) should be something to focus on while performing to give the mind something to anchor.

notes.title: Improvisation and Voice Leading
notes.raw_capture: Harmonic movement can be broken down to what each voice (usually each string on the guitar) is doing between chord changes. When arranging you should consider three parts; melody (top line), bass and the inner voicings.
notes.cleaned_text: Hey there Jonas, Thanks for the great session today. Utilizing your fourth finger (pinky) on your left hand will give you more options for voicing and playing melody. Think about what improvising really is and how this relates to learning a language. Homework: Play a 1-4-5 progression and focus on the top line melody.

notes.title: Technique Overhaul - Blackbird
notes.raw_capture: Right hand technique was the main focus of our session. Ensure that you have your thumb forward and try to align your articulation to attack the string vertically.
notes.cleaned_text: Hey Steve, Great session again today. We focussed more on guitar technique and posture with the goal of improving how you can approach Blackbird as a song. Holding your guitar with a higher and angled 'classical' posture to give your hands easier access to the strings. Rest the bout on your right inner thigh and the waist on your left thigh.
